item.title: 2027: Police will not be used as Political Tool – IGP
item.description: By Edwin Philip Abuja -The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Olatunji Dusu has assured Nigerians that the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) will not serve as a political tool ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dusu was speaking on Tuesday at the day 2 of 2027 edition of Media Development Conference, organised by Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) taking place at the Abuja Continental Hotel, Dusu emphasised that policing is anchored on public trust and accountability rather than force. ​Expressing commitments ahead of the 2027 elections, the IGP stated that the Nigeria Police Force will be guided by professionalism, neutrality, and accountability to all Nigerians, political parties, and the law. ​He said “Any police officer found to be partisan, to have taken sides, or to have aided any candidate or the party will face disciplinary action under the force’s code of conduct”. ​Addressing grievances surrounding the alleged misuse of the Cybercrime Law against journalists, Dusu pledged that the police under his leadership will not be a willing tool for oppression in the hands of politically motivated actors. He warned that elections can now be disrupted through the information environment—via fake videos, doctored audio, coordinated social media falsehoods, and fabricated stories capable of triggering real-world violence. Responding during the panel session which was on ‘People centred public safety and State policing in Nigeria’, the Nigerian Police boss, said that Nigerians should not be afraid of the State Governors misusing the State policing system, he assured that safeguards are being developed to ensure state police structures are not hijacked for personal or political interests, including provisions for federal intervention if situations get out of hand. IGP noted that the National Assembly, and the nation are working to design a framework suited specifically to Nigeria’s realities rather than copying foreign models, emphasising that police training will be standardised across the country so that officers in states such as Lagos and Kano undergo uniform training standards regardless of differing local functions. On the enforcement of the Cybercrime Act, the IGP disclosed that the force has held two symposiums since his assumption of office to examine cybercrime laws and digital offenses. He urged citizens and media practitioners to familiarize themselves with the provisions of the Act, noting that actions often perceived as minor online can constitute offenses under the law. He added that personnel posted to the NPF cyber section are being trained and equipped to tackle emerging digital crimes. IGP Dusu affirmed that journalism is not a crime and described journalists as essential partners in progress and development who hold governments accountable. item.title: Police arrest 11 suspected yahoo boys in Ogun, recover charms
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU), under FCID Alagbon, has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during an intelligence-led raid on an alleged cybercrime hideout, popularly known as a “Yahoo academy,” in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The operation also led to the recovery of suspected fetish materials, including charms, blood-stained items and suspected human remains, alongside 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350. The suspects were reportedly arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following investigations by detectives of the police unit. According to the police, the suspects were allegedly members of an organised internet fraud network known as “Hustle Kingdom”, which operated from the apartment and used the facility as a base for cyber-enabled fraud and other criminal activities. The Police Public Relations Officer of the PSFU, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen, saying preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects exploited the identities and personal information of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online. The statement identified the arrested suspects as Adedolapo Samuel, 25; Timothy Babatunde, 27; Ibrahim Sholete, 30; Torioza Oluwatosin, 30; Yusuf Alabi, 30; Adeyemi Seyi, 32; Tobiloba Oguntoyinbo, 32; Taiwo Mathew, 23; Shoyombo Ayomide, 24; Abayomi Rahmon, 32; and Abolaji Tunji, 28. It, however, disclosed that the alleged leader of the group, identified as Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, popularly known as “Update”, was still at large. The police said Olanrewaju allegedly rented the property in 2021 before recruiting young men into the criminal network. The statement read in part: “Investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju ‘M’, also known as Update, currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation, commonly known as a ‘Hustle Kingdom’, where they use the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities. “The suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.” Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police, Eloho Okpoziakpo, said the operation underscored the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in tackling organised financial crimes and other cyber-enabled offences. Okpoziakpo said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the property and determine whether its owners had discharged their responsibilities by verifying the identities of their tenants and monitoring activities on the premises. item.title: Champions League: Arsenal face tough Dortmund test as Man City welcome Napoli
item.description: Arsenal will face a stern test when they host Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City welcome Italian champions Napoli to the Etihad Stadium as the competition enters Matchday Five. The two fixtures headline Tuesday’s European action, with both Premier League sides seeking important victories to strengthen their positions in the league phase. Arsenal, who currently occupy third position with 10 points from four matches, will be looking to maintain their impressive European run when they welcome Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta’s side have recorded three victories and a draw in their opening four Champions League matches, beating Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague before playing out a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich. The Gunners, however, will be without goalkeeper David Raya, who sustained a shoulder injury during their recent encounter with Newcastle United. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are also listed among their unavailable players ahead of the Dortmund clash. Dortmund, meanwhile, arrive in London in good form after moving to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach at the weekend. The German side have also won three of their four Champions League matches, beating Real Betis, Sabah and Villarreal, although they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt. They currently sit one point behind Arsenal and will be hoping to close the gap with a positive result in London. The encounter will also offer an interesting reunion for Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri, who is spending the season on loan at Dortmund and is eligible to feature against his parent club. Meanwhile, Manchester City will welcome Napoli in another important encounter at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side occupy seventh position with nine points, while Napoli are 27th with three points after winning just one of their opening four matches. City head into the fixture after a 1-1 draw against Fulham in the Premier League, having struggled for consistency in recent domestic outings. They will, however, take confidence from their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in their previous Champions League fixture as they look to strengthen their chances of securing automatic qualification for the round of 16. City will be without Antoine Semenyo, who is sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes remains a doubt. For Napoli, the trip to Manchester presents an opportunity to revive their European campaign after defeats to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto. The Italian side secured a 1-0 victory over Torino in Serie A at the weekend but face a difficult assignment against Guardiola’s men. Former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature for Napoli, adding another interesting storyline to the encounter. item.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. FIFPRO’s German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would “leave a lasting impression” on Musiala and on the club in general. “I believe those in charge have scored a real ‘own goal’ here,” VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement. World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with “every bit of support.” “Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala’s shoulders,” Matthaeus told RTL. “Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment,” he added. – An opportunity for Musiala – For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly. item.title: Mobile Entertainment Growth Raises Fresh Questions About Consumer Safety in Nigeria
item.description: Mobile-first entertainment has become part of everyday life for many Nigerians. A phone can now be a cinema screen, a music player, a social space and, for adults, a gateway to real-money gaming platforms. That convenience is precisely why consumer safety deserves more attention. The shift is not simply about more people using smartphones. It is about how quickly an app, browser page or payment prompt can move someone from browsing to registering, sharing personal information and making a transaction. A few taps may feel routine, but the choices behind them are not always straightforward. For adult users, the sensible question is not just whether a platform looks polished or loads quickly. It is whether the operator is appropriate for their location, whether its rules are clear, how it handles personal data and what controls exist when someone wants to pause or limit their activity. Consumer protection needs to keep pace with the format. Mobile access removes much of the friction that once came with visiting a physical venue, which makes plain information, proper age checks and visible responsible-play tools more important than ever. Nigeria’s mobile reality brings its own questions Nigeria’s digital economy is shaped by mobile use. For many people, a handset is the main route to the internet, rather than a laptop or desktop computer. That puts entertainment, communication, payments and advertising in the same small screen space. It also means conditions vary enormously. Data costs, connection quality, device storage and payment options can differ from one user to the next. A platform that appears simple in a promotional post may involve lengthy terms, automatic settings or data collection that are less obvious on a small display. Digital payments have evolved quickly too. Bank transfers, USSD options, cards and wallet-based services have made online transactions familiar to many adults. Familiarity can be useful, but it can also encourage people to skim past details they would otherwise read. A few consumer questions are worth keeping in mind: Is the service clearly intended for adults aged 18 and over? Is the platform permitted to operate for users in Nigeria or the relevant state? Does it show the operator’s identity, licensing information and contact details? Are payment, withdrawal, identity-check and account-closure rules easy to find? Does the site explain what personal data it collects and why? Age boundaries deserve particular care. Gaming promotion should not be designed to appeal to under-18s, and adult platforms should have meaningful age-gating rather than a token tick-box. Adults with younger people in their household may also want to use device controls and keep account credentials private. Regulation can involve federal and state-level considerations, so broad claims about legality should always be treated cautiously. item.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

item.title: Champions League: Lookman ruled out of Atletico clash, Osimhen’s return uncertain
item.description: Nigerian forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Atletico Madrid’s UEFA Champions League clash against Viking FK, while Victor Osimhen remains doubtful for Galatasaray’s encounter with Aston Villa. The two Super Eagles stars face uncertain fortunes ahead of Matchday Five, with Lookman set to miss Wednesday’s fixture due to injury. According to reports, Lookman will be unavailable when Atletico Madrid face Viking FK on Wednesday, November 25. His absence adds to the Spanish side’s injury concerns, with Marc Pubill and Romero also ruled out. Meanwhile, Osimhen’s availability for Galatasaray’s home encounter against Aston Villa remains uncertain. The striker recently underwent knee surgery after sustaining an injury during Galatasaray’s 2-0 victory over Stuttgart. He resumed individual training on Thursday, November 19, but was not included in the squad for his side’s victory over Samsunspor three days later. His return to action against Aston Villa is therefore not guaranteed. Elsewhere, Moses Usor will be looking to maintain his impressive form for LASK Linz when they travel to face Bodo/Glimt on Tuesday. Samuel Adeniran is expected to lead the attack alongside Usor, who provided an assist in LASK’s hard-fought 2-1 victory over Hartberg on Saturday. LASK currently occupy 16th position with six points and will be hoping to improve their standing with a positive result in Norway. On Wednesday, fellow Nigerians Mubarak Suleiman and Emmanuel Ayaosi are expected to feature when Slavia Prague host Villarreal at the Fortuna Arena. Slavia have endured a difficult campaign, sitting 34th with just one point after four matches. They are yet to record a victory in the competition. Another Nigerian youngster, Christian Nwachukwu, could also feature when Sabah host Spanish giants Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium on Wednesday. The 20-year-old joined the Azerbaijani club from Sheffield United in August and will have an opportunity to test himself against one of Europe’s biggest sides. item.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. item.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

item.title: ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday. Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Lagos. Salami said the exercise would take place between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. in selected polling units across the state. He said it was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify possible gaps or challenges that would be addressed before the 2027 general elections. According to him, the exercise will cover the 245 Registration Areas (RAs) across the state’s 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), with two polling units selected in each Registration Area. He urged residents, particularly eligible voters in the selected polling units, to participate in the exercise to enable the commission to assess the effectiveness of its equipment and electoral processes. The REC said the list of selected polling units would be displayed at the respective local government area offices to enable residents to identify the designated locations. Salami said he had directed all electoral officers in the state to convene stakeholder meetings in their respective LGAs ahead of the exercise. He said the meetings would provide an opportunity to engage political parties and other stakeholders on the importance of participating in the mock accreditation exercise. The REC said the engagements would also help mobilise eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise. He outlined the activities preceding the exercise, saying BVAS configuration would take place on Nov. 25, followed by the training of nominated personnel on Nov. 26. According to him, personnel and devices would be deployed to the selected polling units on Friday, ahead of the exercise. Salami reiterated that the exercise formed part of INEC’s preparations to ensure a smooth and efficient electoral process during the 2027 general elections. item.title: Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest
item.description: By Steve Oko A woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, has been arrested by the Abia State Police Command for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during a confrontation in Aba. The suspect was also accused of attacking worshippers with fireworks at Christ the King Church (CKC), Aba, triggering panic within the church premises. The police said Barkerk was arrested on Sunday, November 22, after a distress call alerted the Ndiegoro Divisional Police Headquarters to an attack on church members by hoodlums throwing explosive fireworks indiscriminately. According to the Command, a patrol team deployed to the scene to restore order apprehended the suspect with fireworks in her possession. However, she allegedly turned violent, assaulted an inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcefully retrieve the recovered exhibits. The police said she was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation. The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this in a statement Monday, condemning the assault as reprehensible and warning against attacks on officers performing lawful duties. She said the suspect would be charged in court after investigation. Chinaka added that normalcy had been restored at the church and its environs, while police monitoring continued to prevent further breakdown of law and order. The Command warned that it would not tolerate assault, obstruction or interference with police officers in the discharge of their duties, urging residents to maintain peace and respect lawful authority. The post Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
item.description: Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday. “I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings,” said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso. “They’re just so scared and praying to God, that they, please change the hearts of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) and let us out,” added the 43-year-old after observing legal procedures of juveniles being processed through the immigration courts. Her appearance at the New York youth immigration court was part of an effort to shine light on the Trump administration’s immigration policy that was supported by newly elected US lawmaker Brad Lander. Lander criticized a “travesty of justice” as cases are sped up while funding for legal representation is cut. In videos uploaded to her 22 million subscribers on YouTube, Ms Rachel, known for her signature pink headband and denim overalls, teaches infants to identify animals, colors, and numbers. On her other social media platforms, she is taking an increasingly vocal stand for children’s rights. She has notably led a fundraiser for the organization Save the Children in support of Palestinian children in Gaza and has backed campaigns critical of US migrant detention centers where children are kept, decrying poor conditions and calling for their closure. Targeted by a smear campaign for her pro-Gaza stance, Ms Rachel said previously that it would be more controversial to say nothing. “I think it’s sad to take someone’s dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong,” she told PBS last year. The post YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum
item.description: …restrains 29 banks By Taiye Agbaje An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on N135.5 billion paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute. Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards. The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds. The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody. The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds. The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order. The amount represents 100 million dollars, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar. Justice Agbaza made the orders on Nov. 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. Law Firm. A certified true copy of the enrolled order by the court was obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja. Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business as Edwards and Partners Law Firm, is seeking recovery of the money pursuant to an indemnity issued by the NGF. The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under an indemnity dated Dec. 20, 2018, issued by the NGF. The indemnity reportedly arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid 100 million dollars to the NGF as a stakeholder. The money was to be held pending the determination of the Federal Government’s liability to Iseghohi-Edwards over legal and consultancy fees. The fees arose from services allegedly rendered in connection with the London and Paris Club loan transaction. Iseghohi-Edwards claimed he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) to represent the 774 local government councils in the London and Paris Clubs’ refund matters. He had instituted Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over the outstanding professional fees. According to his court filings, the Federal High Court, on Feb. 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness of 318 million dollars. The claimant said the government subsequently made a part-payment of 159 million dollars through promissory notes. He contended that the judgment fulfilled the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the 100 million dollars payable directly to him. item.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder diagnosis
item.description: Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career. According to Deadline , Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury , which is scheduled for release later this month. The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion. He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said. Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night. He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges. item.title: Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari
item.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it. Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses. He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public. All Progressives Congress governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23, 2026. Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally. Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said. The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, and Governor Radda Dikko during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State, on Monday, November 23, 2026. Also speaking, Governor Dauda Lawal expressed gratitude to party supporters for their show of solidarity, while commending the people for their resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. He reaffirmed his administration’s resolve to promote inclusive governance, equitable development and sustained engagement with communities across the state. “This crowd speaks for itself; there is very little to say other than to thank Almighty God. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude. “At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said. The APC campaign train is expected to move to other local government areas of Zamfara State as the party intensifies its mobilisation and grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
item.description: …Plans over 10 regional offices ahead of Yuletide By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots. LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi. Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor. He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season. To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement. Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations. He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges. The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis. He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance. item.title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said. Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens. He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence. “I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone. “Enough is enough,” he said. item.title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials. Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled. “There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue. “If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said. The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa. He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures. Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand. He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides. “Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said. The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest. “I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said. He, however, stressed that efforts to improve bilateral relations must not come at the expense of Nigeria’s national interests or the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa. Fani-Kayode expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric targeting Nigerians in the country. He also condemned attempts to portray Nigerians collectively as criminals and drug dealers, insisting that the actions of a few individuals should not be used to stigmatise an entire community. “As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa. “Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. item.title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
item.description: Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him. Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North. He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him. He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details. He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue. His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on. “As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing. The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing. Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice. “We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said. He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said. The post It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege appeared first on Vanguard News .
